title: An inventory
intro: Four steps, one script that grows. The robot gets a bag: an array of item names with a limit on how many fit, functions to pick things up and look inside, and a way to use an item, which heals the robot when it was a potion. The stage shows the bag and, from the last step, the health bar.

steps.title: A bag with room for four
steps.prompt: The bag is an array of item names, empty to start with. Declare a variable at the top of the script (a member variable) called `items` holding an empty array, `[]`, and another called `capacity` holding the number `4`: the most items the bag can take. Nothing goes in yet; this step only gives the robot its bag.
steps.starter:
# The robot's bag: an array of item names, and how many fit.
# Declare both member variables here.
hints: An empty array is written `[]`, two square brackets with nothing between.
`var items = []` and `var capacity = 4`, both at the top of the script.

docs.what: an empty array; items are added later with append

docs.name: var
docs.what: declares a variable; at the top of a script it is a member variable that every function can use

steps.title: Pick things up
steps.prompt: Write `pick_up`, which takes `name` and tries to put it in the bag. If the bag has fewer items than `capacity`, append the name and return `true`. Otherwise leave the bag as it is and return `false`. The buttons beside the stage pick up a potion or a key; the fifth pick-up bounces off.
steps.starter:
var items = []
var capacity = 4

# Write pick_up(name) below.
steps.solution:
var items = []
var capacity = 4

func pick_up(name):
	if items.size() < capacity:
		items.append(name)
		return true
	return false

tests.name: A potion and a key, in that order
A fifth item does not fit

hints: `items.size()` is how many are in the bag right now; compare it with `capacity`.
Inside the `if`: append, then `return true`. After the `if`, at the function's own indentation: `return false`.
return ends the function, so the `return false` line only runs when the if did not.

docs.name: append(value)
docs.what: adds a value to the end of an array

docs.name: size()
docs.what: how many items an array holds

docs.name: return
docs.what: ends the function and hands back a value; true and false are values too

steps.title: Look inside the bag
steps.prompt: Two questions the robot can answer. Write `has`, which takes `name` and returns `true` when that name is somewhere in `items`, otherwise `false`. Write `count`, which takes `name` and returns how many times it appears. Both walk the array with a `for` loop: `has` can return the moment it finds a match; `count` adds one to a counter each time and returns it at the end.
steps.starter:
var items = []
var capacity = 4

func pick_up(name):
	if items.size() < capacity:
		items.append(name)
		return true
	return false

# Write has(name) and count(name) below.

tests.name: has says no to a gem

hints: `for item in items:` visits each name in turn; inside, compare `item == name`.
In has, `return true` inside the loop leaves the function early; `return false` after the loop covers the case where nothing matched.
In count, declare `var total = 0` before the loop, add `total += 1` on a match, and `return total` after the loop.

docs.name: for item in array
docs.what: runs the block once per item, with item holding the current one
true when both sides are the same value; works on text

docs.name: return
docs.what: ends the function and hands back a value

steps.title: Use an item
steps.prompt: The robot's health from the health milestone is back, at the number `60`, together with `heal`. Write `use`, which takes `name`. Find where that name sits with `items.find(name)`; it gives the position, or `-1` when the name is not in the bag. If it is `-1`, return `false`. Otherwise remove that one item with `items.remove_at(position)`, and if the name was `"potion"`, call `heal(30)`. Then return `true`. Using a key removes it and heals nothing.

tests.name: Using a potion empties a one-potion bag
Using what you do not have returns false
Using an item you have returns true
Two potions cannot heal past the limit

hints: Store what find gives you: `var position = items.find(name)`. Then `if position == -1: return false`.
`items.remove_at(position)` takes out exactly that one, even when the same name appears again later.
Compare the name, not the position, to decide about healing: `if name == "potion":` then `heal(30)`.

docs.name: find(value)
docs.what: the position of the first matching item, or -1 when there is none

docs.name: remove_at(position)
docs.what: removes the item at that position; the ones after it move up

docs.name: heal(amount)
docs.what: the function from the health milestone: adds to health, never past max_health

godot: Open Godot and make a new project called Robot Bag.
Create a 2D scene with a Node2D root named Robot, and attach a script to it.
Copy the whole script from step 4 into it: items, capacity, health, max_health and the five functions.
Add a Label child named Bag. Write `func show_bag():` that sets `$Bag.text = ", ".join(items)`, and call it at the end of pick_up and use.
In `func _ready():` call `pick_up("potion")`, `pick_up("key")`, then `use("potion")`. Run the scene (F6): the label reads key.
Add `print(health)` after the use call and check the Output panel: 90.
Try five pick-ups in _ready and print what the fifth one returns: false, and the label still shows four names.
Add a second Label for health and set its text in heal, so the number changes on screen.
